messages.author: 7f9a35501eadc0b8
messages.subject: Cross type "haploid";
parts:
Dear Karl

I recently saw that with the new R QTL version, you added a cross type "haploid".

As I am working with a haploid and so far read the cross in as a BC and already progressed quite a bit in my analysis, I was wondering if my LOD scores could change if I would use the new cross type ''haploid'' now. What do you think…do I have to run everything again using this new cross type?

Thanks for your help.

Best,

Mark

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Cross type "haploid";
parts:
No need to rerun; "haploid" is exactly the same as "bc" except for genotype labels in things like effectplot. 

karl

messages.author: 256c65e083a80aea
messages.subject: Re: Cross type "haploid";
parts:
Dear Karl,

I have carried out a haploid cross and have the data now in a csv file. The markers are sequence variants and are coded with respect to the two strains as A and B and the marker IDs listed as chromosome positions. The question is; is this coding correct given that since 2013 you have a cross type haploid or does one have to resort to the BC workaround and list everything as homozygous for one of the two genotypes in the (Haploid) parents.

Thanks,

William

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Cross type "haploid";
parts:
The actual analysis for the "bc" and "haploid" cross types are the same. The only difference is in the labels on the genotypes in plots such as effectplot() and plotPXG().

karl
